title: Thinking length and the 6-bit core of K4-Core-K6: BF16 core-tensor swaps on fixed traces (G2) and in free generation (G4), with loop checks
question: Does storing K4-Core-K6's 316 core tensors in 6 bits instead of BF16 make the model think longer, on the vLLM fork with a local loader modification?
engines: tpurtell vLLM fork v0.9.2 release image (index sha256:ea0430aa...) + a local loader modification (route b), not a tpurtell release: repro/vllm-k6-loader/ (built image sha256:5fc05b7c...)
checkpoints: zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-BF16 @ f9fed3bb (316 core tensors, ranged copy, loaded by the local loader swap; not published)
hardware: 2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition (300 W); GPU only, experts local, no DGX Spark expert nodes
